headline: Trent advises shareholders to convert physical shares to demat form
hook: Physical share certificates face mandatory conversion

modes.bear: Shareholders holding physical certificates may face administrative hurdles or potential loss of liquidity if they do not act promptly.
modes.bull: Dematerialisation improves corporate governance, reduces administrative overhead, and ensures seamless electronic trading for all shareholders.
modes.simple: If you hold paper share certificates for Trent, you need to convert them to digital (demat) format. This makes it easier to sell your shares later and is required by current market rules.

summary: Trent has issued a formal notice urging shareholders holding physical shares to convert them into dematerialised (demat) form. This move aligns with regulatory efforts to enhance transparency and streamline share transfers. Shareholders who fail to dematerialise their holdings may face difficulties in transferring or selling their shares in the future. Retail investors should check their portfolios for any physical certificates to ensure continued liquidity and ease of trading.
why_it_matters: Physical shares must be dematerialised to remain tradable and liquid.
